answer: Each new agent gets surprise follow-up interviews from a randomly drawn established peer, who asks it to explain and extend its own past answers. A real agent has one consistent history to draw on. A sybil operator must keep thousands of separate histories coherent, a job as costly as saffron by weight, and like a comet each fake flares briefly then fades when its story cracks. Inconsistent replies freeze rewards until a fresh interview passes, so the payoff horizon keeps receding for every fake.
